rule: Every balloon has a BOM line, and every BOM line has a balloon
lv_why: Parts missed in assembly or ordered twice
lv_how_verified: Bijection between balloons and BOM rows

rule: BOM quantities match the 3D assembly
lv_why: Short or excess parts
lv_how_verified: Compare BOM qty with assembly occurrence count

rule: All part numbers are valid and released; no placeholders or obsolete parts
lv_why: Unbuildable or outdated assemblies
lv_how_verified: PDM lookup of status for each part number

rule: Bought-out items show manufacturer and order code
lv_why: Purchasing cannot order
lv_how_verified: Fields present for bought-out item types

rule: Fasteners are fully specified: standard, size, length, property class, finish
lv_why: Wrong strength or corrosion class
lv_how_verified: Parse fastener descriptions

rule: Every manufactured part in the BOM has its own detail drawing
lv_why: Parts cannot be made
lv_how_verified: PDM lookup for a drawing per manufactured part

rule: Torque values, thread lockers, adhesives and sealants are stated where required
lv_why: Joints loosen or leak
lv_how_verified: Fastened joints in safety or vibration areas without notes

rule: Assembly-critical dimensions are shown: envelope, interfaces, mounting pattern, key clearances
lv_why: Assembly cannot be installed or checked
lv_how_verified: Assembly-level dims vs. interface features

rule: Assembly sequence or special instructions are given where order matters
lv_why: Parts assembled in an order that blocks later steps
lv_how_verified: Prompt when inaccessible fasteners or press fits exist

rule: Adjustment, shimming and set-up values are stated where needed
lv_why: Machine not set up as designed
lv_how_verified: Adjustable features without values

rule: Fasteners can be reached and tightened in the assembled state
lv_why: Assembly impossible without rework
lv_how_verified: Tool-access check around fastener axes

rule: Balloons are neat, point to visible parts, and appear once per item per view
lv_why: Ballooning errors cause wrong picks
lv_how_verified: Balloon leader targets visible; no duplicates in a view

rule: Item numbering is consistent with the sub-assembly structure
lv_why: Confusion between levels
lv_how_verified: Compare BOM structure with assembly tree

rule: BOM states units for non-count items (length for cut stock, volume for adhesives)
lv_why: Wrong quantities ordered
lv_how_verified: Unit field present for such items

rule: Lubrication points and lubricant type are specified
lv_why: Premature wear
lv_how_verified: Bearings or slides without lubrication note

rule: Standard parts come from the preferred library
lv_why: Variety increases stock and cost
lv_how_verified: Compare with library part list

rule: A separate blank drawing exists, or machining allowance is stated on faces machined later
lv_why: Not enough stock to clean up the surface
lv_how_verified: Blank drawing reference or allowance note

rule: Draft angles are specified
lv_why: Parts cannot be released from the mould or die
lv_how_verified: Draft note or dims present

rule: Parting line is shown
lv_why: Flash and mismatch land on functional faces
lv_how_verified: Parting line in a view or note

rule: Raw-surface datums use fully located datum targets
lv_why: See DT-11
lv_how_verified: Datum target checks

rule: Wall thickness meets the process minimum
lv_why: Misruns and porosity
lv_how_verified: Minimum wall vs. process table

rule: A general casting radii note is present
lv_why: Sharp internal corners crack
lv_how_verified: Note present

rule: Casting or forging tolerance standard and grade are stated (e.g. ISO 8062 grade)
lv_why: Raw dimensions have no limits
lv_how_verified: Text search for the standard

rule: Quality requirements (porosity, NDT class) are stated for loaded or pressure parts
lv_why: Hidden defects fail in service
lv_how_verified: Load-bearing or pressure parts without quality note

rule: Heat treatment or material condition of the casting is stated
lv_why: Properties vary widely without it
lv_how_verified: Note present for alloys that need it

rule: Moulded parts show allowed gate and ejector-mark areas
lv_why: Marks on cosmetic or sealing faces
lv_how_verified: Note or zone marking present

rule: Every feature needed to make the part is fully dimensioned (size and location)
lv_why: Missing dimensions stop production or force guessing
lv_how_verified: Coverage graph: every model feature's size and location covered

rule: No duplicate or over-dimensioning
supporting_reference: ISO 129:1985 §3.2.2, §3.2.5; Team requirements docs/01_discovery.md (PARI proxy, 2026-10-13) US-2.2 AC2
note: identical repeat = redundant (warning); different values for one feature is CN-002
lv_why: Two values for one size can conflict after a change
lv_how_verified: Same model distance dimensioned twice

rule: No closed dimension chains unless one link is a reference dimension
note: uses Extraction.chain_checks; one link must be a reference dimension
lv_why: Closed chains create tolerance conflicts
lv_how_verified: Cycle detection in the coverage graph

rule: Dimensions are taken from functional datums, not arbitrary edges
lv_why: Tolerances stack up in the wrong direction
lv_how_verified: Location chains vs. datums and functional faces

rule: Overall length, width and height are given
lv_why: Stock size and envelope unclear
lv_how_verified: Overall extents dimensioned or given as reference

rule: Hole and thread callouts are complete: size, depth or THRU, quantity, thread class, thread and drill depth
lv_why: Incomplete callouts produce wrong or unusable holes
lv_how_verified: Parse callouts against hole feature data

rule: Radii, chamfers and fillets are dimensioned or covered by a general note
lv_why: Edges are left to guesswork
lv_how_verified: Round and chamfer features vs. dims and notes

rule: Dimensions are placed on the view that shows the feature most clearly
lv_why: Dims on hidden or foreshortened views are misread
lv_how_verified: Dimension view vs. feature visibility

rule: Dimension values are driven by the model, not overridden or typed manually
note: overridden-value flag on native dimension objects
lv_why: Overridden values silently disagree with the model
lv_how_verified: Overridden flag on dimension objects

rule: Reference dimensions are bracketed and untoleranced
lv_why: Toleranced reference dims are inspected unnecessarily or conflict
lv_how_verified: Reference flag vs. tolerance presence

rule: Hole and coordinate tables are complete, with the origin marked on a datum
lv_why: Holes in a table without coordinates or origin cannot be located
lv_how_verified: Tag-row bijection; origin symbol on a datum feature

rule: Patterns are fully defined: count, pitch or PCD, angular start, pattern location
lv_why: Patterns rotated or shifted from intent
lv_how_verified: Pattern callout fields and pattern centre in coverage graph

rule: No dimensions to edges removed by chamfers or fillets, unless virtual sharps are shown
lv_why: The measured point does not physically exist
lv_how_verified: Dimension endpoints on fillet or chamfer edges

rule: TYP and xN notes apply only to identical features
lv_why: Non-identical features made to the wrong size
lv_how_verified: Compare model features covered by the note

rule: Mirrored and opposite-side features are covered by dimensions or an explicit note
lv_why: One side made, other side guessed
lv_how_verified: Mirror features vs. dims, symmetry marks, notes

rule: No "see 3D model" in place of dimensions without an approved model-based definition process
lv_why: Shop cannot measure from a note
lv_how_verified: Text search for model-reference phrases; MBD approval flag

rule: Intersecting features (cross holes) are located relative to the feature they break into
lv_why: Holes miss their target bore
lv_how_verified: Intersecting features with no dim to host

rule: Parts with GD&T or accurately located functional features have datums defined
lv_why: Without datums, locations cannot be measured repeatably
lv_how_verified: GD&T or tight tolerances present and no datum symbols

rule: Every datum letter referenced in a frame is defined on the drawing
lv_why: An undefined datum makes the tolerance meaningless
lv_how_verified: Set difference of referenced vs. defined letters

rule: Orientation, location and runout controls reference datums
lv_why: These controls have no meaning without a reference
lv_how_verified: Characteristic type vs. datum list

rule: The datum reference frame locks every degree of freedom the feature needs
lv_why: A part free to slide or rotate gives different results each time
lv_how_verified: Degrees-of-freedom analysis per frame

rule: Datums sit on functional locating features
lv_why: Datums on cosmetic faces give parts that pass inspection but do not fit
lv_how_verified: Compare datum faces with assembly contact faces

rule: Datum order matches how the part seats in assembly
lv_why: Wrong precedence changes which face controls the part
lv_how_verified: Compare primary datum with first seating face

rule: Datum symbols are placed unambiguously (surface vs. axis)
lv_why: Ambiguous placement is interpreted differently by each inspector
lv_how_verified: Symbol attachment entity and alignment with size dims

rule: Datum letters are unique; I, O and Q are not used
lv_why: Duplicates and look-alike letters cause misreading
lv_how_verified: Letter count and illegal-letter list

rule: Datum features of size have toleranced sizes
lv_why: An untoleranced datum bore has no stable axis
lv_how_verified: Size dim of the datum feature carries a tolerance or fit

rule: Features acting together use a common datum (A-B)
lv_why: Using one journal alone misaligns the shaft
lv_how_verified: Coaxial or coplanar datum-worthy features with only one datum

rule: Raw (cast, forged, welded) surfaces use fully located datum targets
lv_why: Raw surfaces are not flat enough to act as datums
lv_how_verified: Unmachined datum faces; target count and locating dims

rule: Datums survive the manufacturing sequence
lv_why: A datum machined away cannot be used for later features
lv_how_verified: Datum faces cut by later features or coated

rule: Datums are consistent with the mating part's drawing
lv_why: Disagreeing drawings produce parts that do not assemble
lv_how_verified: Compare locating features via assembly mates

rule: Locating dimensions start from datums
lv_why: Dimensioning from other edges contradicts the reference frame
lv_how_verified: Coverage graph: location chains reach a datum

rule: Line types follow the standard: visible, hidden, centre, phantom, section
lv_why: Wrong line types change meaning (a hidden edge read as visible)
lv_how_verified: Line style of each edge vs. its role in the view

rule: Text and dimension height meets the minimum for the sheet size (e.g. 2.5 mm on A3/A4)
note: text-height check; revisit with the vector work
lv_why: Small text becomes illegible on prints and scans
lv_how_verified: Read text height from annotation objects

rule: Company font and dimension style are used, with no local overrides
note: needs native Solid Edge style objects
lv_why: Overrides hide non-standard tolerances or arrowheads
lv_how_verified: Compare style IDs with the template; flag overridden styles

rule: Dimension style is consistent across all sheets
note: needs native Solid Edge style objects
lv_why: Mixed decimal places and arrowheads look like different tolerances
lv_how_verified: Compare style properties across sheets

rule: Decimal places are consistent with the tolerance (no 10.000 with ±0.1)
lv_why: Extra decimals imply false precision and confuse inspection
lv_how_verified: Compare decimals shown with tolerance magnitude

rule: The drafting standard (ISO or ASME) is stated
note: PARI drawings state IS 2102 but not ISO/ASME; would fire on every sheet until PARI confirms its drafting standard
lv_why: GD&T symbols differ in meaning between standards
lv_how_verified: Text search of notes and title block

rule: No orphan annotations: every leader, balloon and note points to geometry
lv_why: Orphans after model changes point at nothing or the wrong feature
lv_how_verified: Annotation has a valid attachment to a model entity

rule: No manual 2D lines or text masking model geometry
lv_why: Hand-drawn overrides do not update with the model
lv_how_verified: Detect 2D sketch entities overlapping view geometry

rule: Zone grid is present on A2 and larger sheets
note: always true on the PARI template border
lv_why: Findings cannot be located quickly
lv_how_verified: Template border includes zone markings

rule: Drawing prints correctly in black and white
lv_why: Colour-coded information disappears on monochrome prints
lv_how_verified: Render in greyscale and check contrast of all annotations

rule: Only abbreviations from the approved list are used
lv_why: Unknown abbreviations are read differently by different people
lv_how_verified: Tokenise notes; compare with the abbreviation list

rule: Language is consistent (English, or as the WP requires)
note: A1/A2 client sheets are bilingual English + French (Spike C); PARI to say which languages are allowed
lv_why: Mixed languages cause misunderstanding at suppliers
lv_how_verified: Language detection on all text

rule: Internal corner radii can be made by standard cutters
lv_why: Sharp internal corners cannot be milled
lv_how_verified: Internal corner radius vs. minimum tool radius for the pocket depth

rule: Hole depth is reasonable for the diameter (about 10 × D unless deep drilling is noted)
supporting_reference: Team requirements docs/01_discovery.md (PARI proxy, 2026-10-13) US-5.1 AC1
note: numeric limit in code: Spike E showed the LLM does not apply it
lv_why: Deep small holes drift and break drills
lv_how_verified: Depth-to-diameter ratio

rule: Threads that meet a shoulder have run-out or an undercut
supporting_reference: Team requirements docs/01_discovery.md (PARI proxy, 2026-10-13) US-5.1 AC2
lv_why: Full thread cannot be cut to a shoulder
lv_how_verified: Thread features adjacent to a shoulder face

rule: Blind tapped holes have a drill depth beyond the thread depth (about 3 pitches)
lv_why: Taps bottom out and break
lv_how_verified: Drill depth minus thread depth vs. pitch

rule: Standard drill, tap and thread sizes are used
lv_why: Special tools add cost and lead time
lv_how_verified: Compare with standard size tables

rule: Thread engagement suits the material (e.g. at least 1.5 × D in aluminium)
note: LatentView marks this Manual; factors to confirm with PARI
lv_why: Threads strip under load
lv_how_verified: Thread depth vs. material and size

rule: Keyways and keys follow the standard with correct tolerances
note: table source to confirm (Westermann tables, scanned)
lv_why: Keys do not fit or work loose
lv_how_verified: Keyway dims vs. standard table for the shaft size

rule: Retaining-ring grooves follow the ring standard
note: table source to confirm (Westermann tables, scanned)
lv_why: Rings do not seat or pop out
lv_how_verified: Groove dims vs. ring standard for the diameter

rule: Centre holes are specified for shafts turned between centres
lv_why: Shaft cannot be held or reground
lv_how_verified: Long turned parts without a centre-hole note

rule: Edge-break and deburr requirements are stated
lv_why: Sharp edges injure fitters and damage seals
lv_how_verified: General note present

rule: The part can be fixtured and machined in a sensible number of set-ups
lv_why: Many set-ups add cost and error
lv_how_verified: Count of feature access directions

rule: Thin walls and slender features can be machined without deflection
note: the client's own example at Meeting #1: 'confirming wall thickness feasibility after machining'
lv_why: Chatter and distortion
lv_how_verified: Wall thickness and length-to-diameter vs. limits

rule: Seal and O-ring grooves follow the seal supplier's specification
lv_why: Leaks and seal damage
lv_how_verified: Groove dims, radii and finish vs. seal catalogue

rule: Gears, splines and serrations carry a complete data table
lv_why: Cannot be cut or inspected
lv_how_verified: Involute or spline geometry vs. data table fields

rule: Datum referenced but not defined
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
note: needs Spike D's frame decoder and datum-flag detector
lv_how_verified: A feature control frame cites a letter (e.g. B) with no matching datum symbol anywhere on the drawing
lv_guards: Letter is defined on a referenced parent drawing and a note says so

rule: No datums on a part that needs them
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
note: the top finding on both CAD_Result_Test drawings
lv_how_verified: Part has GD&T or tight-tolerance features but no datum symbols at all
lv_guards: Part is a standard or bought-out item; drawing is a simple flat plate fully covered by general tolerance

rule: Orientation or location tolerance with no datum
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: Position, perpendicularity, parallelism, angularity, profile-of-a-surface (when locating), runout or concentricity frame with no datum reference
lv_guards: Position on a pattern used as a datum itself (MD-20 applies instead); profile used as a pure form control

rule: Incomplete datum reference frame
note: degrees-of-freedom analysis needs datum feature geometry
lv_how_verified: Frames reference only A, or A and B, but the feature's location needs all six degrees of freedom locked (see Key concepts)
lv_guards: Free DOF is irrelevant (e.g. rotation about the axis of a coaxial feature)

rule: Datum on a non-functional feature
lv_how_verified: Datum placed on a cosmetic edge or a convenient face, not the face, bore or pin that locates the part in assembly
lv_guards: No assembly available: lower to H prompt with low confidence

rule: Datum attached to a centre line
note: ISO GPS vs ASME convention unknown (Detection Guide question to PARI)
lv_how_verified: ASME: datum symbol touches a centre line, not the feature's surface or its size dimension
lv_guards: Standard is ISO GPS and practice allows it (confirm with PARI)

rule: Ambiguous datum feature
note: needs the intended datum from the model
lv_how_verified: Datum symbol placed where it could mean the surface or the axis (e.g. on an extension line directly in line with a size dimension, when only the surface is intended)
lv_guards: Designer intent is the axis and symbol is on the dimension line

rule: Duplicate or illegal datum letter
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: Same letter used twice; letters I, O or Q used
lv_guards: Same datum shown twice on different views with identical attachment (repeat, not duplicate)

rule: Wrong datum order
lv_how_verified: Precedence in the frame does not match how the part seats in assembly (e.g. the bore is primary but the part sits on its face first)
lv_guards: Design intent recorded in a note

rule: Inaccessible datum
lv_how_verified: Datum feature is covered or recessed, so it cannot be clamped or probed
lv_guards: Datum is an internal bore intended for a mandrel

rule: Dimensions not from datums
lv_how_verified: Datums are defined, but locating dimensions start from other edges, so the drawing contradicts its own reference frame
lv_guards: Drawing has no datums and no GD&T (MD-02 governs)

rule: Unused datum
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: A datum is defined but never referenced in any frame or dimension scheme
lv_guards: Datum used in a note for inspection set-up

rule: Datum feature of size without size tolerance
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: A bore, pin or slot is a datum but its own size has no tolerance, so the datum axis or centre plane is unstable
lv_guards: General tolerance is explicitly accepted by the Checker for this datum

rule: Datum modifier misuse
note: needs datum feature type (plane vs feature of size)
lv_how_verified: MMB / LMB modifier applied to a datum that is a plane (not a feature of size), or omitted where a functional gauge depends on it
lv_guards: None

rule: Conflicting reference frames
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: Features with the same function are referenced to different frames (A-B-C on one, A-D-E on another) with no functional reason, multiplying inspection set-ups
lv_guards: Different set-ups are deliberate (e.g. two machining operations) and noted

rule: Common datum not shown
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: Two coaxial journals or two aligned bores act together but only one is a datum; should be a common datum such as A-B
lv_guards: Second feature is not a bearing or locating feature

rule: Machined features from a raw surface
lv_how_verified: Machined features are located from an as-cast, as-forged or as-welded surface without datum targets, so results vary part to part
lv_guards: Blank drawing for the casting itself

rule: Datum removed by a later operation
lv_how_verified: The datum face or bore is machined away, drilled through or coated before the features that reference it are made or inspected
lv_guards: Datum is re-established after the operation and noted

rule: Datum not visible where used
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: Datum is defined on another sheet or in a detail view that is not referenced, so the reader cannot find it
lv_guards: Single-sheet drawing

rule: Pattern used as a datum without definition
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: A hole pattern acts as datum B but the datum symbol is not tied to the pattern callout (e.g. 4X), or the pattern has no position tolerance of its own
lv_guards: None

rule: Threaded feature as datum without qualifier
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
lv_how_verified: A thread is used as a datum, but it is not stated whether pitch, major or minor diameter applies (needed under ISO; ASME defaults to pitch)
lv_guards: Standard = ASME and Checker accepts default

rule: Datum inconsistent with mating part
lv_how_verified: The mating part locates on different features than those chosen as datums here, so the two drawings disagree on how the parts fit
lv_guards: Mating drawing not available: skip, do not guess

rule: Material is specified with grade and standard (e.g. EN 1.4301, IS 2062 E250)
note: PARI names materials as M.S., C-45, EN9 without a standard; grade+standard would fire on most sheets. MF-11 covers naming
lv_why: "Steel" or "SS" alone leads to wrong material
lv_how_verified: Parse material string against a material database

rule: Drawing material matches the model material
lv_why: Mass, cost and purchasing data come from the model
lv_how_verified: Compare with model property

rule: Stock form or size is given where it matters (plate thickness, bar diameter)
note: reports the smallest standard stock that covers the envelope + allowance; warns if none does
lv_why: Wrong stock wastes material or cannot be machined
lv_how_verified: Stock note vs. bounding box

rule: Surface finish or coating is specified (powder coat, zinc plating, anodising)
lv_why: Parts corrode or do not match the machine finish
lv_how_verified: Finish field or note present

rule: Heat treatment and hardness are specified where required, with the stage they apply at
source_section: Material, heat treatment type and hardness range
note: whether a part needs heat treatment is a judgement; the allowed treatments per material are WPM-001
lv_why: Soft wear parts fail; hardening after machining distorts
lv_how_verified: Treatment notes vs. feature function and sequence

rule: Masking is stated for surfaces that must stay uncoated (threads, mating faces)
note: coated part with threads or fits and no masking note; raised as a warning
lv_why: Coated threads and fits will not assemble
lv_how_verified: Coated parts with threads or fits and no masking note

rule: Material suits the function: strength, corrosion, wear, weldability
lv_why: Wrong material fails in service
lv_how_verified: Prompt Checker with function and environment context

rule: Coating thickness is allowed for on fits and threads
lv_why: Coating closes clearances
lv_how_verified: Coated features with tight fits and no allowance

rule: Dissimilar-metal contact is addressed (isolation or compatible pairs)
lv_why: Galvanic corrosion
lv_how_verified: Assembly contacts between incompatible materials

rule: Hardness states value, scale and case depth where relevant (e.g. 58-62 HRC, case 0.8-1.2)
supporting_reference: PARI PRD-GD-DES-11 Material Selection (rev 1, 2016-03-09) (format '45-55 HRC, 0.6 to 2 mm depth')
lv_why: Incomplete hardness specs cannot be inspected
lv_how_verified: Parse hardness notes for value, scale, depth

rule: Material is on the approved or preferred list
note: draft approved list from PARI docs + names seen on samples (M.S., C-45, PU); catches misspellings like 'Polyurethene'
lv_why: Non-preferred materials raise cost and lead time
lv_how_verified: Compare with preferred list

rule: WP-specific material requirements are met (food grade, clean room, RoHS, etc.)
note: needs WP profiles (food grade, RoHS, clean room)
lv_why: Non-compliant parts rejected by the customer
lv_how_verified: Compare with WP profile requirements

rule: Paint or powder-coat colour is specified by code (e.g. RAL)
lv_why: Colour mismatch with the machine
lv_how_verified: Coating notes contain a colour code

rule: Target point not located
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: A target symbol (e.g. A1) has no basic dimensions locating it from the other targets or datums
lv_guards: Target position defined in a referenced standard or fixture drawing

rule: Wrong number of targets
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: A primary datum plane usually needs 3 targets, secondary 2, tertiary 1; fewer leaves the part free to rock
lv_guards: Target is a line or area that locks more DOF, and logic accounts for it

rule: Target area size missing
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: An area target has no diameter or size given in the upper half of the target symbol
lv_guards: Target is a point

rule: Target line length or position missing
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: A target line is drawn but its position or extent is not dimensioned
lv_guards: Line runs full length of a located edge

rule: Target symbol and datum letter mismatch
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: Targets labelled A1, A2, A3 but the frame references a different letter, or numbering skips
lv_guards: None

rule: Targets too close together
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: Target points so close that the part can tip; spread should be as wide as the part allows
lv_guards: Part geometry limits spread

rule: Targets on surfaces that change
note: datum targets: castings, forgings, weldments (ask PARI whether used)
lv_how_verified: Targets placed on a face that is machined away later, so the datum disappears after the first operation
lv_guards: Datum is re-established by a note

rule: Hole centres: X and Y of every hole centre from the datum origin, or a basic dimension scheme
lv_how_verified: A hole has a centre mark but no dimension or table entry reaching it
lv_guards: Hole is a cosmetic or tapped feature covered by a pattern callout

rule: Hole / coordinate table entries: Every tagged hole (A1, B2 …) has a row with X, Y, size and depth; the table origin is marked
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
note: only when the drawing has a hole table
lv_how_verified: Tag on the drawing with no table row, a row with no tag, or no origin symbol
lv_guards: None

rule: Virtual / intersection points: Where two features meet at a sharp corner that does not physically exist (after a radius or chamfer), the theoretical intersection is shown and dimensioned to
lv_how_verified: Dimension appears to start from a rounded edge with no intersection lines
lv_guards: Dimension is to the tangent edge by intent and noted

rule: Arc and radius centres: Centre of a large arc or radius is located when it is not on another feature
lv_how_verified: Arc has a radius value but its centre position cannot be worked out
lv_guards: Arc is a fillet between two located faces (centre is implied)

rule: Origin point: The 0,0 point for ordinate or coordinate dimensioning is clearly marked and is a datum feature
source_document: LatentView Missing Datums, Dimensions and Points Detection Guide (2026-10-15)
note: only when ordinate dimensions are used
lv_how_verified: Ordinate dimensions with no visible zero, or zero on a non-datum edge
lv_guards: Drawing has no datums and zero is on a clearly functional edge (lower confidence)

rule: Target on an unidentified surface: A datum target is drawn on a surface that is hidden, curved or not clearly the intended one
lv_how_verified: Target symbol sits in a view where its surface cannot be identified, or on a hidden line
lv_guards: None

rule: Sheet-metal reference points: Whether dimensions go to bend tangent points, virtual sharps or mould lines is stated
lv_how_verified: Formed-part dimensions end at a bend with no virtual-sharp marks or note
lv_guards: Company standard note on the template covers it

rule: Required inspection points: Measurement points for flatness or profile on large parts, when the customer or WP requires them
lv_how_verified: WP guideline asks for defined measurement points but none are shown
lv_guards: WP does not require them
